blocks.title: Clustering
blocks.text: Clustering groups similar things together by their characteristics. K-means is one of the simplest and most popular methods: we choose the number of groups, K, and the algorithm groups points by their distance from cluster centres.

items: Choose K = 2: one cluster for students stronger in Math, one for students stronger in English.
Place initial centres: Basim (85, 70) and Tallat (40, 85).

Assign each student to the nearest centre using Euclidean distance. Umer is 7.1 from Basim; Anie is 11.2 from Tallat; Maliha is 26.9 from Basim and 32.0 from Tallat, so she joins Basim. Cluster 1 is Basim, Umer, Maliha; cluster 2 is Anie, Tallat.
Recalculate each centre as the average of its members: cluster 1 (78.3, 65), cluster 2 (45, 82.5).
Repeat assigning and recalculating until the centres stop moving. Here nobody changes cluster, so the result is stable.

blocks.text: Euclidean distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is the square root of (x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2; for Maliha and Basim it is the square root of 25^2 + 10^2 = 725, about 26.9.
